messages.subject: Re: why does SEM in lavaan use z-value instead of t-value?
parts: Why does lavaan use not use and also may someone enlighten me why lavaan uses z-value instead and how I can maybe support that if I use it in my thesis?

ML and least-squares estimators for SEMs rely on asymptotic theory, i.e., their behavior is known (when assumptions are met) as N approaches infinity.  Sampling distributions of SEM parameters are asymptotically normally distributed, so Wald z scores are reported.  If you can figure out which df parameter is appropriate for a particular parameter, one could in principle account for finite-sample behavior by using an appropriate t distribution.  But I imagine that must be quite difficult, since no one (to my knowledge) has been able to derive such a df parameter.

You might get a more enlightened answer on the more general forum SEMNET (since this is not a software question anyway):

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html
